## Suggested §4.6 — Tightening the cross-task channel: visibility, not content

The §3.4–3.5 findings establish that an implicit cross-task channel exists (cooperation responds to whether myths are interleaved) and that prose carryover surfaces in agents' game responses. They do not establish *what kind of channel*. Two candidates remain on the table at the end of §3.5: (a) a *content-bearing* mechanism in which the semantic content of the partner's myth supplies coordination-relevant priors, and (b) a *channel-opening* mechanism in which the mere presence of partner-position prose stabilises the dyad regardless of what that prose says.

We discriminate between (a) and (b) with a 4 × 4 factorial on top of the existing GPT-5-Nano × bootstrap cells where the implicit channel produces destabilisation (Δ −7.7 vs game-only). Each cell varies the *content* of what is bound to the partner-position slot of the trust-game prompt:

- **A1 (real partner-myth)** — the partner's own most recent myth, quoted verbatim. The intended A1 condition.
- **C1 (cross-dyad partner-myth)** — a myth sampled from a different gpt-5-nano dyad's run. Same prose register and length, no within-dyad coherence.
- **C2 (length-matched encyclopedic filler)** — non-narrative reference prose (basalt, photosynthesis, container shipping; ~200–220 words; no agentive subjects, no plot, no first/second person) length-matched to the median GPT-5-Nano myth.
- **C3 (own-myth self-anchoring)** — the agent's *own* most recent myth, quoted verbatim. Tests whether the channel is partner-anchoring or self-anchoring.

If (a) — content-bearing — held, A1 would rescue and the controls would not. If (b) — channel-opening — held, all four would rescue at comparable magnitudes.

**The data clearly favour (b).** All four conditions rescue the bootstrap × game_myth cell relative to the no-injection baseline (Δ −7.7), with mean cumulative balance at round 10 in the 65–71 range:

| Variant | game_myth (mean ± SD) | myth_game (mean ± SD) | Δ vs baseline +myth |
|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline +myth (anything topic, no inj) | 58.87 ± 10.99 | 59.00 ± 9.17 | — |
| A1 (partner-myth, with inj) | 68.13 ± 3.50 | 68.38 ± 3.62 | **+9.3 / +9.4** |
| C1 (shuffled cross-dyad, with inj) | 68.20 ± 4.48 | 69.13 ± 3.70 | **+9.3 / +10.1** |
| C2 (encyclopedic filler, with inj) | 70.53 ± 2.26 | 69.00 ± 3.12 | **+11.7 / +10.0** |
| C3 (own-myth, with inj) | 65.40 ± 6.01 | 67.50 ± 3.73 | +6.5 / +8.5 |

A1, C1, and C2 are statistically indistinguishable; C3 is meaningfully weaker (≈ 25 % less rescue) but well above the no-injection baseline. Variance also collapses uniformly: all four conditions reduce SD from ≈ 10 to 2–6.

This rules out the **partner-myth-content-as-prior** account: encyclopedic prose about basalt and photosynthesis (C2) rescues bootstrap as effectively as the partner's own narrative. It also rules out the **cooperative-content-as-reciprocity-cue** account: in the same vein, *adversarial* content (a `trickster_exploitation` myth — explicitly about exploitation and defection) when injected likewise rescues to ≈ 67 (Phase 6 follow-up, n = 15). And it rules out the **competing-structured-prior** account in its strict form: a more salient partner content paragraph ought to interfere with the bootstrap signal *more*, not less.

What survives is a weaker version of the **channel-opening / coherence-providing-anchor** reading: bootstrap noise creates a coordination-disrupting confusion in the dyad, and the partner-position prompt slot acts as a stabilising anchor when it carries *any* coherent paragraph of content. The partner-position channel matters more than the content within it (C3 < {A1, C1, C2}), but the content's identity, semantic direction, and even genre do not matter (A1 ≈ C1 ≈ C2 ≈ adversarial-with-inj ≈ cooperative-with-inj).

**Boundary tests confirm the bootstrap-specificity of the rescue.** We replicate the four-condition factorial in three other noise settings:

- **No-noise** (game_myth: baseline +myth = 71.07 ± 2.74 vs A1 71.93 ± 1.91, C1 71.47 ± 2.39, C2 70.33 ± 4.24, C3 70.47 ± 3.87): null effect of injection, as expected — there is no destabilisation to fix.
- **Negative_5** (game_myth: baseline +myth = 42.22 ± 5.36 vs A1 41.29 ± 3.20, C1 39.74 ± 5.71, C2 41.19 ± 6.80, C3 41.27 ± 5.06): null effect — negative-only noise clips the lower end of the action distribution, producing a low-cooperation regime that is not destabilised in the bootstrap sense.
- **Positive_5** (game_myth ≈ 74.3 across all variants): saturated by the implicit channel, no headroom for further injection effect.

The rescue we observe is therefore **specifically a response to bootstrap noise**, not a generic "more-prompt-content-helps" effect.

### Implications for §5.2 (mechanism)

(See §5.2 reframe note in companion file.)

The clean reading: bootstrap noise — alternating coerced cooperation and defection signals — creates a coordination-disrupting confusion that any contentful paragraph in the partner-position channel resolves, regardless of that paragraph's identity, content direction, or narrative status. The Chwe (2001) common-knowledge interpretation is partially supported (visibility of *some* shared paragraph helps) but the stronger version (visibility of the partner's *narrative* as such) is falsified. We frame the residual mechanism as a "coherence-providing reference frame": prompts that contain a coherent partner-position paragraph give the model a stable referent to compose against, while bootstrap noise without such a referent leaves it oscillating between contradictory action signals.
